MONOTONE BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY COMPARISON, and the construction is the security argument. load_signed_manifest takes min_version as an ARGUMENT and hands the accepted version back 'for the caller to record'; nothing recorded it, so the floor was 0 on every start and an attacker who could serve an old manifest could un-revoke a root, re-widen a closed overlap window, or resurrect a withdrawn issuer. Rollback protection that resets on restart is not rollback protection.

THE SINGLE-COUNTER DESIGN HAS TWO FAILURES AND THE TOPOLOGY IS MULTI-WRITER. Two writers that both read floor 5 and persist 10 and 7 leave it at 7, making a superseded manifest acceptable again. Writing through one fixed .tmp path is worse: every writer truncates the same inode and writes from its own offset, so 100 and 7 publish as 700 — rejecting every legitimate manifest until an operator repairs the file by hand. A max over a set that only GROWS has neither failure.

DELETION IS A CHEAPER CAPABILITY THAN CORRUPTION, and an ephemeral sidecar loses its volume on every restart, so '0 after deletion' would hand back the whole rollback window for free. The operator-declared bootstrap minimum is the part of the floor an attacker cannot reach.

UPWARD IS THE TUF FAST-FORWARD SHAPE. The markers are unauthenticated by construction, so a directory writer can pin the floor at u64::MAX and refuse every manifest including a break-glass revocation. The ceiling FAIL-STOPS and never clamps: min(stored_floor, ceiling) would be WORSE than no ceiling, because it lowers a floor on the say-so of the storage that just proved untrustworthy, silently re-opening the rollback window and letting the attacker choose which versions come back by choosing how far to overshoot.

NOT AVAILABILITY: a malicious fast-forward still stops the client. What is established is that it stops LOUDLY, at a named error, rather than silently withdrawing every anchor once the loaded manifest expires. AND THE CEILING IS WORTH EXACTLY THE TRUST DOMAIN IT COMES FROM — read from a config file the floor-directory writer can also edit, it adds nothing.
